newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - June 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Chevron Corp and partners Texaco, Mobil and Shell, will announce shortly a huge deal to develop the Gorgon Gas Field off the coast of Western Australia. As part of the deal, gas will be piped to the North-West Shelf onshore facility for conversion into liquefied natural gas. Page 1.

Following the release of a Cash Economy Taskforce report yesterday, Taxation Commissioner Michael Carmody said the Australian Tax Office would look for innovative strategies to target the "black" economy, which is worth up to A$6 billion a year in uncollected tax revenue. He said traditional methods had failed and the new strategy would focus on educational programmes and incentives to report cash transactions. Page 3.

Australis Media Ltd will seek a full merger with Optus Communications Ltd's pay-TV business after a court ruling last week cancelled a joint venture satellite agreement between the companies. Should a merger go through, the resulting entity would have great power, with control of almost all content across cable and direct-to home delivery services. Page 21.

Competition regulator Professor Allan Fels will today warn of the possible limiting of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's role in consumer protection, with the Wallis Committee's recommendation that a single regulator should be responsible for conduct in the market and disclosure in the financial sector. Fels will also warn of ACCC plans to monitor any mergers between life insurance and superannuation companies. Page 21.

The Ainsworth family, who control Aristocrat Leisure Ltd, may have laid the plans to allow unhappy family members to offload their stakes by cancelling a pre-emptive rights agreement over each other's shares. There are concerns that fights over the family's interests will prompt some members to offload their holdings. Page 21.

The events surrounding last week's dramatic rise of Cultus Petroleum NL shares only a day before the company announced an oil discovery are being investigated by the Australian Stock Exchange. There is concern over a briefing given by Cultus executives to stockbroking analysts on Wednesday of last week. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Foster's could announce a share buy-back as early as tomorrow as it disperses almost A$2.5 billion of stock held by BHP and Japanese brewer Asahi. It is believed Foster's will distribute the stock as widely as possible to a range of institutional buyers, with the federal government taking a strong interest in the scheme. Page 21.

Six weeks after opening for business, the re-named Sizzler chain, Bells Restaurants, has closed, leaving 1,600 workers jobless. Owner Universal Food Holdings has been placed in voluntary administration after paying A$60 million to acquire 39 Sizzler Restaurants in four states in April. Page 21.

Trading in Cultus Petroleum has been halted by the Australian Stock Exchange while further information is sought on the estimated reserves of a new oil discovery off the coast of Western Australia. The exchange has sought an explanation after contradictory statements were made by partners Cultus and Shell on the likely reserves. Page 21.

Federal Court Justice Murray Wilcox has labelled the actions of ICI Australia as "ludicrous" and "lamentable" in seeking the registration of a cotton pesticide in the late 1980s. Wilcox was dissatisfied with ICI's Australian researchers who did not check whether cotton crop remnants were fed to cattle. Page 23.

A special task force has been set up to work with Comalco and Chevron on the development of projects worth over A$3 billion. Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge says the agreement has "signalled" the potential for a long-term economic boom. Page 23.

Ariadne is set to purchase Kings Parking and Pacific Parking for A$12.6 million, following the A$25 million sale last week of its pathology services investment. The deal will be subject to shareholder approval and a report by independent expert Ernst & Young. The purchase is the first for Ariadne since 1987, when it recorded a record A$600 million loss. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Talks have commenced between Telstra and News Corp to end Telstra's cable roll-out that may result in the communications group paying compensation of several hundred million dollars. Telstra chief executive Frank Blount and Foxtel and News director Ken Cowley are expected to negotiate an agreement to release Telstra from its current roll-out deal. Page 25.

Secretary to the Treasury Ted Evans has told a Senate committee that real estate rates in Australia were high when measured against world standards, due to expectations about high inflation. Evans said there was a clear link between interest rates and high expectations of inflation. Page 25.

KPMG corporate finance director Antony Cohen believes the New South Wales electricity generation industry could reach a lower sale price than the Victorian power industry, but NSW distribution companies may attract multiples similar to those paid in Victoria. Cohen denied claims that power station sales would lead to job losses. Page 25.

Two of Victoria's leading credit unions, Advantage and Piccol Community, will announce a merger today to form the state's biggest credit union with total assets of A$500 million. They will seek member approval to join under the Advantage banner. The merged credit unions would serve 110,000 members, and Advantage chief executive officer Rob Nicholls has given assurances that none of the group's 225 staff would lose their jobs, and no branches would close. Page 27.

Australis Media could face cash flow problems by August following the Federal Court's decision to ban a satellite joint venture with Optus Communications. Australis stood to receive benefits of A$150 million from the deal. Australis has played down the effects of the court decision, saying it would force Optus to consider a merger. Australis has also been have merger talks with Foxtel, and will be under intense pressure to secure a deal in coming weeks. Page 27.

Macquarie Bank yesterday revealed a 25.4 percent increase in annual net profit to a record A$117 million, and a 32 percent rise in total assets under management to A$23.5 billion, bettering most stockbroking analysts' expectations. The bank promised more increases thanks to continuing boom conditions in financial markets this year. Page 27.
THE AGE

Telstra chief executive Frank Blount has held meetings with News Ltd executives on ending Telstra's obligation to install a broadband cable network to four million homes. Telstra may end the deal at a cost of several hundred million dollars, but it is believed this option will require the approval of Kerry Packer's PBL. Page B1.

The Macquarie Bank has announced a record annual profit of A$116.9 million, boosted by an increase in funds under management. Chairman David Clarke says favourable conditions in 1996/97 are expected to continue in the current year. Page B1.

Building approval figures released yesterday have shown that total dwelling approvals have risen by 3.6 percent seasonally adjusted, with market economists predicting the figures will lessen the chances of another interest rate cut. The Housing Industry Association believes the market is on the move with rate cuts now beginning to take effect. Page B1.

Prime Minister John Howard has dismissed calls for a freeze on car tariffs, and is set to announce further cuts. The Coalition party room is divided on the issue, with a compromise to be found between industry calls for a stop to tariff cuts, and an Australian commitment to remove trade barriers by 2010. Page B1.

Diversified industrial group Hancock and Gore yesterday announced a record interim net profit of A$2.45 million for the six months to March 1997, representing a 16 percent rise in net profit. The group predicts another record profit for the year to September with HGL chief executive Kevin Eley saying each of the company's core operating businesses are improving despite challenging external conditions. Page B2.

Investment group Ariadne Australia has agreed to buy the car parking businesses Kings Parking and Pacific Parking, in Brisbane and Sydney, for $A12.65 million - just over four times the A$2.7 million operational earnings returned by the businesses, before finance charges, last year. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
